Pele Yoetz 62:2: Behold, the category of mitzvah - this comes out first: Torah study outweighs them all (Pe'ah 1:1). Every mouth that increases study in Torah finds life; great is Torah, for it gives life in this world and in the World to Come (Avot 6:7) - for great is study, which leads to practice (Kiddushin 40b) and to all unity and all perfection in traits and opinions, and its special property is that it is a seasoning against the evil inclination and burns away the impure spirit from a person, purifying and sanctifying him. And therefore a person's inclination overpowers him greatly to keep him idle from Torah, for it knows that this is its own undoing. And come and see how far the power of the evil inclination extends - for a person sits and speaks idle or forbidden words all day and all night without growing tired, yet when he sits to study even one hour, he grows tired and it becomes as heavy as a burden to him. Tell me, please, what extra trouble or expense is there in words of Torah more than idle words? On the contrary, everyone knows that whoever occupies himself with Torah enjoys the fruits in this world while the principal remains for him in the World to Come, and gives peace of mind to his Maker - even if he repeats all day the verse "and Timna was Lotan's sister" (Genesis 36:22), for every time he repeats it, the Holy One, blessed be He, establishes reward for him (Tanna D'Vei Eliyahu, ch. 2). Correspondingly, for idle and forbidden words he is destined to give an account even for light conversation - this is nothing but evil of heart, for the inclination of a man's heart is evil from his youth, sin crouches at the door, and causes even a child to flee from school. But whoever has understanding shall take to heart that the Holy One, blessed be He, created the evil inclination for man's own good, so that he overcome his inclination and receive reward - for in overcoming his inclination he gives peace of mind to his Maker. Therefore he must overcome his inclination to be diligent in study at every free moment, even against his own will and to his own displeasure, until he becomes accustomed - and in the end the evil inclination itself becomes hollow within him, and it becomes sweet and pleasant to him.
Pele Yoetz 62:3: Second, speech of mitzvah is the voice of prayer, the voice of supplication. Greater is prayer than sacrifices (Berachot 32b). And this refers not only to the fixed prayers, from which one cannot be exempt, but also that for every trouble that should not come, whether trouble of money or trouble of body or trouble of soul, one must offer prayer before the trouble, or cry out and pray over the trouble that has come - for so the King of the universe has established, that He desires prayer and longs for the prayer of Israel, and reverses the decree, rising from the throne of judgment and sitting on the throne of mercy through prayer. And prayer is good both before the decree and after the decree (Rosh Hashanah 16a). And greater is prayer than good deeds, for Moses was answered only through prayer, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 32b) - and all the more so we, orphans of orphans, since we have become so impoverished of good deeds and have multiplied transgression and lack all good - on whom shall we rely if not on our Father in Heaven, who is appeased by mercy and grasped by supplications, and hears the prayer of every mouth? Whoever cries out with tears of the heart, with a broken and crushed heart, it is possible to say of him, "and clean" - He shall cleanse him of every trouble and distress, for the LORD, our Shepherd, our Father, our King, shall wait to be gracious to us through our prayers.
Pele Yoetz 62:4: (And now I recall that the master, author of Sefer "Charedim," a pure man, has already gathered all the mitzvot from the words of the Torah and the words of the Sages that depend on speech, and all kinds of transgressions from Torah law and the words of the Sages that depend on speech - and I shall follow after him and copy his holy words with a small addition, with the help of Heaven, and shall abbreviate somewhat. Let the wise man hear and increase learning, and from this, praise on high shall be rendered - for this is my whole desire and longing, and may the LORD God help me for the sake of the honor of His Name.)
Pele Yoetz 62:5: It is a mitzvah from the Torah to honor one's father and mother, and one's father's wife and one's mother's husband, and one's father's brother and father's sister, and one's mother's brother and mother's sister, and one's father's father and father's mother and mother's father and mother's mother, and one's father-in-law and mother-in-law and one's older brother, and one's teacher, and whoever is greater than oneself in wisdom - to all of these one is obligated to give honor in speech, each according to his own honor, for the obligation is not equal for all of them. And honor in speech consists of speaking to them calmly and with a gentle tongue and honor, as one speaking to a king - and even if one of these becomes angry with him and disgraces him and reviles and curses him to his face, he shall answer them with appeasement and words of conciliation, "sweet as a honeycomb, pleasant words" (Proverbs 16:24). And by this Isaac our father recognized and said (Genesis 27:22), "the voice is the gentle voice of Jacob." And this is the trait of a good person to practice with every person, all the more so with one to whom he is obligated in honor, and especially to his father and mother - for our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Yerushalmi Kiddushin 1:7) that whoever speaks harshly to his father or mother, even if he feeds them fattened chickens, inherits Gehinnom, may the Merciful One save us. Therefore everyone who trembles at the mitzvah of the God of Israel shall keep his eyes open for every kind of honor, and especially to speak to them in a language of honor for the honor of the King of glory.
Pele Yoetz 62:6: It is a mitzvah to recite ten remembrances with the mouth (I shall write below under the entry "Zichronot" [remembrances]), as brought in the prayer books. And although once a day suffices, nevertheless whoever increases in reciting them is praiseworthy and performs a mitzvah. And each one has branches, and anything similar to them is like them - for example, the mitzvah of remembering the exodus from Egypt is not limited to the exodus from Egypt specifically, but rather all the kindnesses and wonders of the LORD that He performed, whether for Israel as a whole or for individuals, whether for oneself or for others - whoever recounts them performs a mitzvah, and this is the master theme of the Book of Psalms, and comes as a warning many times: "remember His wonders" (Psalms 105:5); "make known His deeds among the peoples" (ibid. verse 1), and many such verses. And the prophet said (Isaiah 63:7): "I shall recount the kindnesses of the LORD." And all of it turns to one place - to recognize the essence of His power and providence, blessed be He, and His love and compassion, and to arouse love and fear.
Pele Yoetz 62:7: And likewise regarding remembering the Sabbath and the standing at Mount Sinai - not specifically that, but rather if he remembers the goodness of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the abundant good He bestowed upon us, in that the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to bring merit to Israel and multiplied for them Torah and mitzvot, the just ordinances of the LORD - we have no greater kindness than this - this speech too shall be counted a mitzvah. And likewise regarding remembering the manna and that He gives strength - not specifically that, but rather whatever a person remembers and recounts of the kindnesses of the LORD, who prepared his livelihood, whether by natural means or beyond natural means, he performs a mitzvah. And likewise regarding remembering Amalek - included in this is to remember that he creates destroyers to corrupt and adds strength to the Other Side through his ugly deeds, and causes the Holy One, blessed be He, to be unable to remove the dominion of arrogance, and the Name is not complete and the Throne is not complete - and through this, one's heart shall be moved to repent, and this is also the intent of the mitzvah of confession, and it is also included in the mitzvah of "remember that which you provoked." And it is likewise included to remember and recount that He has not dealt with us according to our sins nor repaid us according to our iniquities.
Pele Yoetz 62:8: And in remembering what Balak and Balaam schemed to do to our ancestors is included remembering and recounting how, in every generation, individuals or many rise up against us, whether against the individual or against the many, to destroy us, and the Holy One, blessed be He, saves us from their hand. And in remembering the deed of Miriam the prophetess is included remembering and recounting rebukes for sin, for many are the pains of the wicked, so that children shall tremble. And in remembering Jerusalem is included remembering and recounting how much distress in Heaven and distress to all the worlds we cause through our sins.
Pele Yoetz 62:9: This is the general principle: whoever speaks something that causes fear or love of the LORD, and keeping every good thing and withdrawing one's hand from doing any evil, and returning in repentance and the like, performs a mitzvah - provided he directs his heart to Heaven. And in this manner, those who fear the LORD shall speak when in the company of people, and reveal their own conversation to teach the people the benefit that comes from these words, and through this the conversation of their lips shall be esteemed, accepted, and pleasing according to all that comes forth and according to the benefit that follows from it - so shall it be pleasing.
Pele Yoetz 62:10: It is a mitzvah to bless the LORD with the blessings over enjoyment and the blessings of mitzvot and thanksgivings, calmly and aloud, with intention and with joy of heart.
Pele Yoetz 62:11: It is a mitzvah upon the priests to bless Israel. And how foolish are those priests who go out to the synagogue courtyard so as not to recite the priestly blessing, thereby losing much good - three things: performing a positive mitzvah, and being blessers from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written (Numbers 6:27), "and they shall put My Name upon the children of Israel, and I shall bless them." And it is good in the eyes of the LORD that every person bless Israel, and whoever blesses is himself blessed, as it is written (Genesis 12:3), "and I shall bless those who bless you." And all the more so for the righteous - as soon as one mentions them, he is obligated to bless them, as it is written (Proverbs 10:7), "the memory of the righteous is for a blessing." Behold, therefore, one must be careful, when mentioning Abraham our father or other righteous and pious men throughout the generations, to say "peace be upon him," or "may his memory be for a blessing," or "may his memory be for life in the World to Come" - and it shall be counted a mitzvah. And I am amazed that I have not seen people accustomed to being careful about this when mentioning the names of the early Tannaim, Amoraim, and Geonim, while when mentioning the names of the later rabbis, whether in writing or in speech, they are careful to immediately say "may his memory be for life in the World to Come" or "the memory of a righteous and holy man be for a blessing" - and as it appears, it would be more fitting to be careful for the ancient holy ones, whose littlest finger was thicker than the loins of the later ones, to fulfill in their case the verse (Proverbs 10:7), "the memory of the righteous is for a blessing" - namely, to bless them or recount their praise.
Pele Yoetz 62:12: It is a mitzvah to recite the Shema in the morning and evening, and every time one remembers the unity of the LORD and accepts the yoke of His kingship and His love and accepts the yoke of His mitzvot - and likewise when one speaks of these matters, he fulfills the equivalent of the mitzvah of reciting the Shema.
Pele Yoetz 62:13: It is a mitzvah to judge, instruct, and inform the people of the statutes of God and His teachings, and to save an oppressed person from his oppressor. And included in this is to rebuke and protest against transgressors as one can, whether through blessings or requests. And it is a mitzvah to debate with a Torah scholar to bring out a true judgment in its truth, and likewise to debate with one's fellow if he has sinned against him, not to bear a grudge and hate in the heart but to say to him, "why do you do so" - and through the debate, peace shall increase. But regarding this matter it is said (ibid. 9:8): "do not rebuke a scoffer, lest he hate you" - for if he is a forceful and powerful man who does not accept his words, let him not rebuke him, but rather forgive him in his heart and that suffices; but if he sees that he sins or walks in a bad way, he is obligated to rebuke him first with a gentle tongue and in private, and if he does not listen, let him rebuke him even openly and with force, up to striking - and through this the man is cleared of sin, and even if his words bore no fruit, he receives his reward for not having withheld good.
Pele Yoetz 62:14: It is a mitzvah upon whoever knows testimony for his fellow to testify in court, in a manner that the judgment come out truthfully through his testimony. And included in this is to speak whatever can benefit one's fellow with words, whether regarding his money, his body, or his soul, or to give him peace of mind and relieve him of his sorrow and grief - and included in this is good tidings, and informing him of harm about to come upon him and correcting it with good counsel as far as his own intellect can reach. And included in this is to comfort and console one who is in distress, and to gladden a bridegroom and bride, and to appease the poor and the sick, and to bring them back in repentance, and to remind them of every mitzvah matter, and to pray for them and for everyone who is in distress, and to eulogize every deceased person and recount his praise, whatever good is found in him, and to make peace between a man and his fellow and between a man and his wife, and to greet every person first with peace, and to seek their welfare and their good - and any such thing, whatever is spoken to cause benefit and peace of mind to one's fellow, shall be counted a mitzvah for him.
Pele Yoetz 62:15: It is a mitzvah to answer "Blessed be He and blessed be His Name" and "Amens" and "may His great Name be blessed" and "and bless" properly, in clear speech and with the heart's intention. And likewise it is a mitzvah to recite Kiddush and Havdalah over wine, and to read the Megillah, and to recite Hallel. And likewise to praise the LORD and give thanks to everyone from whom one has received benefit for every kind of good, and to sing before the LORD and praise Him with pleasant conversation, to honor the LORD from the grace He has graced us with. It is a mitzvah to praise the righteous and recount their praise and the praise of their good deeds. And it was written in the name of the master Rabbi Yisrael Ba'al Shem Tov, that whoever speaks the praise of the righteous is considered as though he occupies himself with the mystical Account of the Chariot. Correspondingly, it is a mitzvah to speak of the disgrace of publicly known wicked men and the disgrace of their evil deeds, so that people distance themselves from the deeds of the wicked and cleave to the deeds of the righteous. It is a mitzvah to eulogize every night the destruction of the Temple and the exile of the Shechinah with a voice of wailing. And it is a mitzvah to confess and pour out conversation to seek forgiveness from the Master of masters. These and similar things are all good things, all beloved, and they have branches, and in whatever direction they turn, the heart's intentions are the essentials - whatever is intended for the sake of Heaven, both these and those are the words of the living God, and in them the God-fearing man shall meditate. But it has already been stated that the one who chooses shall choose between good and lesser good, and Torah study outweighs them all, and everything depends on the occasion and the time - there is a time for every desire. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, already said (Tanchuma Beshalach 9) that Israel is likened to the silkworm, whose mouth makes garments for kings - so the Jewish man can, through his mouth, build his chambers in heaven and give peace of mind to his Maker, and prepare for his soul the garments called the "robe of the Rabbis."
Pele Yoetz 62:16: And the permitted category is what a person is necessarily obligated to speak for the need of his livelihood and the repair of his body. And in this one must minimize and speak briefly, and of this it is said (Berachot 61a): "let your words" (meaning, what is for your own need) "be few." And especially when one must speak with a woman, one must minimize and shorten greatly, for we learned (Avot 1:5): do not engage in much conversation with a woman - "with his own wife" they said this (Niddah), all the more so with another's wife. And Rabbi Yose HaGelili, because he said to a certain woman, "by which road shall we go to Lod" - when he could have shortened it and said "by which [road] to Lod" - she called him "foolish Galilean" (Eruvin 53b). But when he speaks what is necessary, without any admixture of forbidden speech, and shortens and rises above it, then it is permitted. And whoever's every deed is for the sake of Heaven and occupies himself only with what is necessary for the need of God, blessed be He, then all his deeds and all his speech are counted as mitzvot. And whoever has the Name of Heaven fluent in his mouth over everything he does and says is like alchemy, which turns lead into silver - so this one turns every optional deed into a mitzvah, for just as preparation for the Sabbath is itself a mitzvah, so every preparation for the service of God, blessed be He, shall be counted a mitzvah (as written under the entry "Hachanah" [preparation]).
Pele Yoetz 62:17: And this too, speech that mentions the Name of Heaven, is itself speech of mitzvah, and it is the [formula] that goes before ["for the sake of the unification..."], which must precede every deed and every speech, whether of mitzvah or of the permitted - for even mitzvot require intention, and it is even more necessary to mention the Name of Heaven regarding a mitzvah matter than regarding a permitted matter, for the Kabbalists wrote that the husk always desires to attach itself to every deed of the Jewish man, and by mentioning the Name of Heaven, one separates the husk so that it cannot attach itself.
Pele Yoetz 62:18: And therefore in a mitzvah matter, sanctify it - and especially in mitzvot that have an element appealing to the evil inclination, where there is physical enjoyment, such as the pleasure of the Sabbath and the joy of a festival and the mitzvah of marital relations and the like, there is a great desire for the husk to attach itself to holiness and take a portion in it, for this is its own sustenance, in the manner of what is written (Psalms 12:9), "the wicked walk about on every side." And this causes a person to go out of line and do things not for their own sake, and especially in the mitzvah of marital relations, the grip of the husk is very evil, for it causes an evil soul for the child. And the remedy for this is that he precede every single deed he does and every word he speaks by saying:
Pele Yoetz 62:19: "For the sake of the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, I hereby come to fulfill this mitzvah to give peace of mind to our Former and to repair matters at their root in the supernal place. And let there be favor," and so on.
Pele Yoetz 62:20: And if he comes to say this again, before the Torah blessing, he shall repeat it and say, "and let Your favor be upon us," and so on - and through this the Other Side no longer has permission to attach itself and grip that mitzvah, even if he does not perform it entirely properly for its own sake. It ascends and rises on high, for speech comes and brings forth from thought, and one mitzvah draws another - if regarding optional matters his own ears shall hear what his own mouth utters, saying that he does it for the need of the service of God, blessed be He, then how can he increase beyond the need, and how can he neglect the service of God, blessed be He, to do that deed, and how can he mix a prohibition into that deed? It is found that deed comes and brings forth from speech, and the One who dwells in the heavens laughs at him. Therefore one must take care to do things properly, by measure, by weight, and by measure of capacity.
Pele Yoetz 62:21: And likewise regarding a mitzvah matter, by saying "for the sake of the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah," he shall come to be aroused to fear and to love. To fear - thinking, woe is me, for my sins have overwhelmed my head, and I am concerned lest my sins withhold the good from me and I not be worthy that the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah be unified through me. And see the Holy Zohar, Parashat Shemini (page 37), that the death of Nadab and Abihu was because they were not worthy that the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah be unified through them, since they were not married. And let the man also tremble and be seized lest his deeds not be worthy to ascend for favor and peace of mind before our Father in Heaven because of his sins, in the manner of what is written (Psalms 50:16), "and to the wicked God said, what right have you to recite My statutes?" And also because of his own lack of intention, that he does not know and does not intend the intentions that are fitting to intend - and through this his heart shall be humbled and he shall reflect on repentance, and shall perform the mitzvah properly in every way he can, perhaps he shall be accepted. And he shall also be aroused to love, thinking: happy is the one born of woman, whose foundation is in dust, who merits and has it in his power to bring about the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, and to give peace of mind to the King of the universe - this is a great kindness beyond compare, and it is impossible not to rejoice, and he shall perform the mitzvah with great joy.
Pele Yoetz 62:22: And the forbidden category is very large in its camp, and we shall begin first with the mitzvah category, for we have explained several prohibitions relevant to the mitzvah of Torah study. Whoever is wicked and does not reflect on repentance - his Torah goes to the husk and adds strength to the Other Side, and therefore it is said (Psalms 50:16), "and to the wicked God said, what right have you to recite My statutes and take My covenant in your mouth?" Therefore one must reflect, before every study and every prayer, that he regrets completely everything with which he has provoked his Creator - and even though he shall return to his evil way, in the manner of their saying, of blessed memory (Nedarim 9b), that the wicked are full of regrets, nevertheless whoever regrets from his heart and soul has performed and benefited, so that his prayers ascend for favor before the LORD. And how good it would be for him to be accustomed to say with his mouth, before every study and every prayer: I hereby regret completely everything with which I have provoked my Creator, and I desire with a whole heart and a willing soul to return in complete repentance and to serve my Creator a complete service, a perfect service. Help us, God of our salvation, for the sake of the honor of Your Name, and so on.
Pele Yoetz 62:23: Whoever interrupts his study and says, "how beautiful is this tree," is liable for his own soul and is fed coals of broom bushes (Avot 3:7). And it is written in Sefer Chasidim (944) that one who studies and, in the middle of his study, interrupts to speak idle words or gaze at women, is punished even for the study itself. And alas for those who are found not careful of this, so that they inherit a double Gehinnom, may the Merciful One save us. Therefore one must be very careful, and especially if he said before studying, "for the sake of the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah" - for if he is not careful, he is a slanderer who separates a master [i.e., separates the divine unity]. And if he must speak, let him close the book as though he had finished his study, and afterward return to study anew - perhaps through this there shall be a gap and it shall be considered clean [of the interruption's consequence].
Pele Yoetz 62:24: The Torah is called a potion of life (see Avot D'Rabbi Natan 34:10; Eruvin 54a; Kiddushin 30b) - "it is a tree of life to those who grasp it firmly" and a potion of death to those who deviate from it. And the Torah is likened to a governor who has the power to kill and to give life - so too the Torah has the power to kill and to give life (Shabbat 88b), such as one who studies in order to provoke and be arrogant, for whom it would be better had he not been created. And it is because of this sin that Torah scholars are found who wound one another in halachic debate and speak or write words of provocation against one another, and accusation and hatred multiply among Torah scholars - and if the flame of division has fallen among the cedars, what shall the hyssop of the wall do (Mo'ed Katan 25b)? And the man who desires life shall occupy himself with Torah for its own sake, and shall be God-fearing and acknowledge the truth, accepting the truth from whoever states it, and shall not be a lover of victory who turns to arrogance and those who stray into falsehood (Psalms 40:5), establishing his own words through forced interpretations - and he shall not say "accept my view" even if it seems to him that the truth is with him, and shall not hold fast to a dispute to overturn his fellow's words, but rather state his own opinion once and not repeat it to him - and when he speaks his words, even if his fellow defies him, he shall answer him with a gentle tongue and love and affection, and shall lower himself even before one who is smaller than himself, like a student arguing before his teacher - for our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Bava Metzia 85b): "the small and the great are there" (Job 3:19) - whoever makes himself small over words of Torah becomes great in the World to Come. And through this, he who offers his cheek to the one who strikes him shall be sated with the disgrace of the one who struck him.
Pele Yoetz 62:25: And the straight path for every author of a composition is that he write his own opinion and not raise his lips to refute another's words - but if it is relevant for practical legal purposes, let him refute the opposing proofs in an offhand manner, and merely write at the end, "see such-and-such a book," letting the reader choose. And regarding matters of exposition, let him answer "acknowledged, acknowledged," whether it is good or bad, for what does it matter - and especially in the presence of laymen, great care is needed among Torah scholars to show honor to one another in speech and deed. And if he sees that his fellow is greatly grieved were he to win the argument in the presence of laymen, since he is concerned for his own perceived honor, he shall withdraw so that it appears his fellow has won, and shall receive reward for the withdrawal - and when they are alone together, the two of them, he shall repeat his own point and reveal his opinion. These are some of the ways of men of sound judgment, so that their Torah be pleasing.
Pele Yoetz 62:26: Regarding the mitzvah of prayer as well, if he prays while drunk, so that he cannot speak properly before the King (Eruvin 64a), or while he needs to relieve himself (Berachot 23a) - and likewise one who speaks words of Torah or a legal matter or a mention of the divine Name in the bathhouse, or while naked, or facing nakedness, or in a place that is not clean of filth - his prayer is an abomination, for he does not discharge his obligation and his blessings are in vain, and in a mitzvah matter he commits a transgression, forced to speak carrion-like words. And even if he is not so drunk or does not so urgently need to relieve himself, whenever he has drunk or needs to relieve himself, even though he discharges his obligation, he commits a transgression, and it is found that he performs a mitzvah and a transgression together.
Pele Yoetz 62:27: Whoever speaks in the middle of prayer, or in the middle of the Shema, and even during Pesukei D'Zimra or during the repetition of the Amidah, or in the middle of Hallel and the like, and likewise whoever speaks or engages in laughter and levity or raises his voice in the synagogue, showing that he has no reverence for the sanctuary - his punishment is great, as brought above.
Pele Yoetz 62:28: Whoever recites prayers and blessings without intention, while knowing how and being able to intend, is like a body without a soul - even though he discharges his obligation and receives reward for the mitzvah, he shall be punished for reciting it without intention, as it is written (Isaiah 29:13): "because this people draws near with its mouth, and honors Me with its lips, while its heart is far from Me, and their fear of Me is a commandment of men learned by rote - therefore I shall again do a wondrous thing with this people, a wonder and a marvel," and so on, may the Merciful One save us - and it is as though he had spoken both good words and bad words, of which the good is accepted and the bad is not.
Pele Yoetz 62:29: Whoever recites vain blessings, or unnecessary blessings, or blessings rushed or garbled, or facing nakedness, or in a place that is not clean, for "the word of the LORD he has despised" (Numbers 15:31) - in a mitzvah matter he has a transgression in his hand.
Pele Yoetz 62:30: Whoever rebukes his fellow in public and shames him has, in a mitzvah matter, a transgression in his hand, as though he had shed blood (Bava Metzia 58b). And likewise one who rebukes in a place where it is not fitting to rebuke, for there is a time to speak and a time to be silent - such as in a place where they said, "leave Israel alone, better that they sin unwittingly" (Shabbat 148b, Beitzah 30a, Bava Batra 60b) - and if he makes them willful [by pointing out the prohibition], he shall be punished. And likewise one who argues after peace has already been concluded, thereby reviving the dispute, in the manner people say: an argument is half a division.
Pele Yoetz 62:31: Whoever renders a halachic ruling in his teacher's presence without his permission, even something as trivial as an egg in gravy (Eruvin 62b), or renders a ruling while drunk (ibid. 64a), or renders a ruling on a matter not clear to him as [the prohibition against] his own sister (Sotah 22a) - in a mitzvah matter he has a transgression, and he shall be punished for it, for "many are those it has felled slain, and mighty are all its victims" (Proverbs 7:26). And whoever is brazen in rendering rulings is [in fact] lowly of spirit and coarse of spirit, while whoever is among those who fear to render rulings is diligent and rewarded.
Pele Yoetz 62:32: Whoever answers an orphaned Amen, or a rushed or clipped one, and likewise in answering "Amen, may His great Name be blessed" and the like - in a mitzvah matter he has a transgression in his hand.
Pele Yoetz 62:33: "One who blesses his fellow with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him" (Proverbs 27:14) - as we wrote above under the entry "Berachot" [blessings], namely such as when he blesses him in front of others and causes many to pounce upon him [expecting similar treatment].
Pele Yoetz 62:34: Whoever recounts a person's praise in the presence of his enemies, or in the presence of people who are not free of slanderous talk, shall be counted against him, for through his praise it comes to his disgrace. And likewise, whoever speaks a person's praise to his face in a manner that could cause him to become arrogant - in a mitzvah matter he has a transgression in his hand, for he transgresses "and before the blind you shall not place a stumbling block" (Leviticus 19:14) (as written below under the entry "Shevach" [praise]).
Pele Yoetz 62:35: Whoever confesses without any heart and without submission - God shall be angry at his voice, and shall say, "she has raised her voice against Me, and you have had the forehead of a harlot" (Jeremiah 3:3). And especially those who stand without bowing their heads, but rather with erect posture, and say the confession hastily, striking their fingertips upon their chest - this is exactly like one who bears malice toward his fellow and says to him, "now you shall see." Rather, the confession must be said with a bowed head and a weeping voice, as written under the entry "Vidui" [confession].
Pele Yoetz 62:36: These are some matters that one thinks to speak in order to receive reward for the speech, yet his hope is disappointed - for some of them, instead of reward there shall be ruin, and joy turned to sorrow, since he thought to perform a mitzvah and instead committed a transgression and an abomination; and some bring their reward, but it is a voice and its breaking [i.e., diminished] - "the place of righteousness, there was wickedness" - deficient in "aroy" [pleasantness] and found instead "srot" [troubles] and distresses, receiving punishment where he expected good reward, for the Holy One, blessed be He, is not lenient nor does He shortchange, God forbid.
Pele Yoetz 62:37: And now we shall begin to mention the portions of speech that are entirely evil, of which the man who fears the LORD must be careful.
Pele Yoetz 62:38: Slander [Lashon Hara] is the root that bears gall, for it is equated with idolatry, forbidden sexual relations, and bloodshed (Arachin 15b), and King David, peace be upon him, has already cut it off, as it is written (Psalms 12:4): "may the LORD cut off all smooth lips, the tongue that speaks great things." And slander is one who speaks in disparagement of his fellow - if it is something untrue, it is also called spreading a bad name; and if it is true, it is called slander whenever it was not already publicly known and this person reveals it - "he who goes about as a talebearer reveals a secret" (Proverbs 11:13) - one who bears tales, going about and bringing things, saying "so-and-so did such-and-such to you," or "he spoke thus and so about you." Great is their sin, for their tongue is a sharpened arrow and their throat an open grave. But if he sees that harm shall come to his fellow, he is obligated to reveal it to him so that he guard himself - of this it is said (Leviticus 19:16): "you shall not go about as a talebearer among your people, nor shall you stand idly by the blood of your fellow; I am the LORD."
Pele Yoetz 62:39: Vulgar speech destroys the soul of those who speak it, as it is written (Isaiah 9:16): "therefore the LORD shall not rejoice over their young men, nor have compassion on their orphans and widows, for every mouth speaks vileness," and so on. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Shabbat 33a) that Gehinnom is deepened for both the speaker and the one who hears and remains silent, and even if a decree of seventy good years was sealed upon him, it is turned to evil for him. And vulgar speech is one who speaks of matters between a man and his wife, whether in plain speech, or by hint, or in the leftover coarse speech of gentiles - and immediately forty angels excommunicate in Heaven whoever brings forth vulgar speech from his mouth, may the Merciful One save us, Amen.
Pele Yoetz 62:40: A false oath or a vain oath - namely, swearing unnecessarily when a court has not required him to swear - or one who mentions the [divine] Name in vain in whatever language - his sin is great, for the whole world trembled at the moment the Holy One, blessed be He, said "you shall not take [My Name in vain]" (Shevuot 39a). And it is forbidden to say of one who is accustomed to swearing over everything that he transgresses "before the blind" [by encouraging a habit likely to lead to a false oath] - but there is a case where it is a mitzvah to swear, such as to satisfy the mind of those who suspect him of something not true, in order to be clean before the LORD and before Israel, or to swear in order to keep his soul from a prohibition, or to strengthen himself to fulfill a mitzvah, as we have written in its place.
Pele Yoetz 62:41: Flattery - namely, when one's mouth and heart do not match, showing excessive affection while his inner self does not match his outer appearance, and all the more so if he speaks peace with his mouth while setting an ambush within his heart - this is an evil trait and brings wrath into the world forever. And the trait of the flatterer is as loathsome as menstrual impurity, and one transgression draws another, for it is not protested by whoever has the power to protest, and the transgression is called by his own name.
